Check draft requirements

Review sample output

Choose what would trigger a second review. Examples include a new workspace, a different data source or a change to the buyer offer. Write the trigger beside the decision it affects. Decide whether the offer fits your work

Begin with the part of the workflow that matters most. Do you need the same user, source data, stored projects or export settings over several weeks? Ask the provider to show the exact workspace and walk through your highest-priority task. Keep the discussion specific. Compare the access period with your real project schedule. If the work needs to be reviewed next month, check whether the source material and output will still be available. If you can use a sample without connecting a production website, store, account or customer file, start there. When reviewing pricing, use the amount and billing conditions shown at checkout. Take into account setup and review time. Frequently asked questions

What should I test first with Wrytly?

Use the same example for both. Write down the intended result, the time available for review and any export or permissions required. If one option provides a demo, check that it is the same product and version you would receive. Include manual steps and the time needed to complete them when you decide which plan fits.

Keep a dated version of the inputs and the accepted result. Include the account or workspace version if it affects the outcome. Add a sentence describing what would justify rechecking the work. For a sample writing workspace, use the evidence you collected to show why the final decision was made.

What if the test output differs from what I expected?

Check whether the example, account or settings changed. Review your source records to see whether the original expectation was supported. Use the smallest correction that addresses the issue and repeat the test under the same conditions. If you still cannot explain the difference, ask the provider about the specific step or feature that failed.

Can I use a shared workspace for ongoing client work?

Confirm who can access saved projects, whether data can be exported and whether you can retrieve the finished material after the access period. Use public or approved sample inputs for an initial trial. If the project involves private client documents or advertising accounts, follow the client’s access requirements and use an arrangement that supports them.
